title: NeuroWare presents neuromorphic computing evidence to UK Parliament during Evidence Week 2026.
summary: On 2026-07-06 in Westminster, NeuroWare Director Tony Kenyon and researchers from UCL and the University of Manchester met with Members of Parliament as part of 'Evidence Week'. The team discussed brain-inspired computing opportunities, policy recommendations for lower energy consumption systems, and highlighted UK leadership. Parliamentary staff received training on scrutinising neuromorphic evidence. Sense about Science organised this annual event to facilitate direct engagement between researchers and legislators regarding AI sovereignty and technology policies.
tldr: NeuroWare presented neuromorphic computing developments and policy briefings to UK Parliamentarians during Evidence Week 2026 in Westminster.
evidence: NeuroWare Director, Tony Kenyon, was joined by Latisha Gordon and Aysha Asif Riaz from UCL, and Andre van Schaik from the University of Manchester, in Westminster on 6 July 2026 to meet Members of Parliament
the team discussed the opportunities offered by neuromorphic computing, presented policy recommendations and highlighted the need to review current policies

NeuroWare presented its findings to... Eleanor Underwood (Parliamentary Assistant for Baroness Hayter), and Sophie Thorley (Parliamentary Adviser to Julia Lopez MP) and Varuna De Silva (Thematic Lead - AI and Digital for UK Parliament)
Professor Tony Kenyon said: 'Brain-inspired, or neuromorphic, computing is a potentially transformative future computing technology that the UK currently leads'
Evidence Week in Parliament 2026... opened with an in-person reverse select committee hearing where constituents asked MPs about the evidence behind policy issues
